title: Flask Debug Mode Enabled in Production - Information and Code Disclosure
description:
Flask debug mode is enabled in production. When accessing the /logout endpoint, a full Werkzeug debugger page is displayed with extensive sensitive information including:

1. Complete Python stack traces revealing file paths and internal application structure
2. Source code of the vulnerable logout handler visible in the error page
3. Werkzeug EVALEX enabled (confirmed by "EVALEX = true" in debugger JavaScript)
4. Different SECRET keys exposed in the debugger page (e.g., "GiYYFL2f9rIsTZcMatu3")
5. File paths leaking internal server directory structure (/home/daytona/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/app.py)
6. Flask application source code visible in error frames showing the logout implementation
7. PIN-protected interactive debugger console accessible without authentication

The Werkzeug debugger console can be unlocked with the PIN, allowing arbitrary Python code execution on the server. The debugger exposes all internal Flask application state, local variables, and source code.
impact:
CRITICAL - An attacker can:
1. View complete source code of the application and all imported libraries
2. Understand application architecture, security measures, and business logic
3. Extract all secrets and credentials hardcoded in the source code
4. View all environment variables and configuration settings
5. Gain remote code execution by unlocking the debugger console (if PIN obtained or bruteforced)
6. Extract sensitive data from the application (database paths, API endpoints, user information)
7. Conduct sophisticated targeted attacks using knowledge of the application internals
8. Compromise the entire application and potentially the underlying infrastructure

This is one of the most dangerous configurations in a production environment, allowing complete application compromise.
evidence:
POC Execution Output:
- [VULNERABLE] Werkzeug Debugger page detected
- [CRITICAL] EVALEX enabled - arbitrary code execution possible
- SECRET key exposed: SECRET = \"GiYYFL2f9rIsTZcMatu3\"
- File path disclosed: /home/daytona/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/app.py
- [VULNERABLE] Application source code visible in debugger page
- [VULNERABLE] Found logout function definition in error page
- Error Type: TypeError: sequence item 1: expected str instance, NoneType found
- [VULNERABLE] PIN-protected debugger console detected

The POC successfully demonstrates:
1. Unauthenticated access to the Werkzeug debugger page via a triggered 500 error
2. Disclosure of sensitive secrets and file paths in the error response
3. Visible source code of the application handlers
4. EVALEX functionality enabled for code execution with proper PIN authentication
remediation:
1. Disable Flask debug mode in production immediately:
   - Change app.run(debug=False) in production code
   - Set FLASK_ENV=production environment variable
   - Remove debug=True from any production deployment configuration

2. Remove Flask app secret key from source code:
   - Move secret key to environment variables: os.environ.get('FLASK_SECRET_KEY')
   - Use a secure secrets management system (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, etc.)
   - Never commit credentials to version control

3. Implement proper error handling:
   - Use Flask error handlers to catch exceptions gracefully
   - Return generic error messages to users without stack traces
   - Log detailed errors server-side only (not visible to users)

4. Use a production WSGI server:
   - Deploy with Gunicorn, uWSGI, or similar production servers
   - Never use Flask's development server in production
   - Configure the WSGI server to disable debug mode

5. Implement centralized error logging:
   - Set up Sentry, ELK Stack, or similar for debugging
   - Log errors with full details server-side
   - Remove local debugging tools from production

6. Secure the deployment environment:
   - Implement security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP)
   - Use HTTPS/TLS for all communications
   - Restrict access to debug endpoints if temporarily needed

7. Incident response:
   - Immediately rotate all Flask secret keys used in this application
   - Audit logs to determine what was accessed through the debugger
   - Change all database credentials and API keys if they were exposed
   - Update all secrets that were visible in debug pages

8. Security headers to add:
   - X-Frame-Options: DENY (prevent clickjacking of debug page)
   - X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
   - Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, OWASP A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration, OWASP A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures, CWE-215: Information Exposure Through Debug Information, CWE-489: Active Debug Code, Flask Security Documentation: https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/2.3.x/security/
toolCallDescription: Documenting critical Flask debug mode vulnerability with working POC that demonstrates information disclosure via Werkzeug debugger page
